messages:
Sam: Quick sync - I'm drafting the RFC for per-route quota headers. Main question: how should SDKs treat 429s when we return both Retry-After and a soft/hard hint?

Ada: My take: keep Retry-After for compatibility. But we do want a way to say "this is a gentle nudge" vs "stop sending". Need a clear SDK behavior.

Jeremy: Agreed. Proposal: always include Retry-After (seconds). Add X-Quota-Soft: true|false and X-Quota-Hardened: true|false. Also include X-Quota-Remaining and X-Quota-Limit. Old clients see Retry-After and behave conservatively.

Lena: For SDK semantics I suggest: 
1) If 429 + Retry-After => pause until now+Retry-After and then retry once automatically.
2) If 429 + X-Quota-Soft=true but no Retry-After => treat as recoverable: apply polite backoff (start 200ms, exp backoff capped at 5s), surface as RecoverableQuotaError, do not fail immediately.
3) If repeated 429s escalate to HardQuotaError after 3 attempts.

Maria: Also need bucket/scoping info in headers for observability and to support per-route vs account buckets. Suggest: X-Quota-Bucket: route:chat:short and X-Quota-Scope: route|account and X-Quota-Reset (unix ts). Example header set we plan to document:

```
Retry-After: 3
X-Quota-Soft: true
X-Quota-Hardened: false
X-Quota-Remaining: 12
X-Quota-Limit: 100
X-Quota-Reset: 1700000000
X-Quota-Bucket: route:chat:short
X-Quota-Scope: route
```

Sam: That example is helpful. One backwards-compat edge: older SDKs ignore custom headers, but will honor Retry-After only if they parse it. So the Retry-After must be present whenever we want any client to pause.

Ada: What about putting richer hints in the response body, e.g. {"quota_hint":"burst_exhausted_until=1700000000"}? Body changes are heavier for clients though. Headers should be first-class. Body hints can be optional in new API versions.

Jeremy: Streaming endpoints are trickier. We may need to emit a trailing header frame (HTTP/2 or HTTP/3) or a final event with the quota headers, then close the stream. SDKs should map that to a StreamQuotaError and surface any X-Quota-Bucket metadata. We'll add this to the streaming SDK checklist.

Lena: Small SDK implementation notes: feature-flag the new header parsing (quota-headers-v2) so we can roll out gradually. Default to legacy behavior when flag disabled. Also expose an event hook so application developers can observe Retry-After and bucket info.

Maria: Monitoring note: please update dashboards to chart X-Quota-Remaining and ratio of X-Quota-Soft vs X-Quota-Hardened responses. Alert if Hardened spikes across many clients.

Sam: Ops/back-end question: when do we return Hardened vs Soft? My thought: Hardened for high-impact regressions or sustained overcommit; Soft for short-lived or opportunistic bursts. Backend teams will map their rate limiter policies to those flags.

Jeremy: Runtime mapping: we can flip X-Quota-Hardened when a route is in a protective mode. Also include X-Quota-Reason header for debugging (short token like overloaded-cache). Keep reason short and optional.

Ada: Are the header names final? X-Quota-* seems fine for now to avoid spec churn. We can revisit later if we want to standardize.

Sam: Next steps: I'll write RFC with header definitions, SDK behavior table, streaming handling, and rollout plan. @Lena will own SDK changes, @Jeremy will own runtime mapping, @Maria will own monitoring updates. Ops: please gate rollout behind feature-flag and canary first.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout 03/07 02:00 UTC. Feature-flag: quota-headers-v2.

Lena: Ack. I'll add a short README in SDK repo and a RecoverableQuotaError class. Also ensure the default exponential backoff parameters are configurable by users.

Maria: I'll update dashboards and add an alert on Hardened header spike. Also make a note to include X-Quota-Bucket in logs to aid investigations.

Sam: Thanks everyone. I'll drop the RFC link here when it's ready. :thumbsup:
